comment: Layers (CLAUDE.md rule 5). A folder in `pure` may not import any module in `banned`, nor a folder in `renderFolders`. `banEverywhere` lists text that no file under src may contain. `owners`: a field of the game's state and the one file that may change it ({ field, owner, what }); every field of simulation state gets a row when it is made (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

banEverywhere.why: every random number comes from a seed (@futuremagic/core Rng)

owners.what: the seed of a match's wind swings and gusts
a match's wind force on the Beaufort scale
the mean bearing a match's wind blows from
the seed the sea's wave sets are drawn from
the sea's swell from elsewhere, drawn once with the sea
how many wave sets the sea has made (each draws its own seed)
the sea's wave sets and when each fades in
how a ship lies on the water: her centre, heading, heave, pitch and roll (floating, N2.2)
the seed every random number of a match comes from (made once by startMatch)
a match's wind (made once by startMatch; its swings and gusts are a function of time)
the match's clock: steps since it began, 30 a second
the match's sea, moved on each step as it follows the wind (its own fields are sea.ts's)
the ships of a match, each stepped once a step
how a ship sails: her heading, way, leeway, helm, what the helmsman steers, her canvas and her yards (N3.3)
how far open each of her doors is
the captain's body on her decks
her doors as the captain has swung them

what a ship has been told to do: her course or full and by, her canvas, hove to, masts aback, the acts still to be done and the orders being carried out (N3.4); at quarters, the shot, the aim, how her guns fire and the captain's word (N5.3a); the orders for her life: the pumps, fire party and wreckage parties and what the carpenter's crew does first (N6.3); strike the colours asked and struck (N6.4)
the ways shut on a ship: a ladder under wreckage, a jammed door, a shroud shot away (N4.2)
the oblongs of a ship's floors no body can cross: a gun run in, a fallen spar (N4.2)
counts the changes to what is shut, so men on their way know to look again (N4.2)
a man on his way: what his route is built from, how far along it, his haste, standing aside, held up or stuck (N4.2; its own fields are going.ts's)
what the route of a man on his way is built from: its two ends, its links, what was shut (N4.2; the route itself is found again, not kept)
the leg of his route a man on his way is on (N4.2)
how much of his leg a man on his way has behind him (N4.2)
a man standing aside for the captain (N4.2)
how long a man on his way has been held up (N4.2)
a man with no way open to where he is going (N4.2)
a ship's crew: every man's task and where he is (N4.1)
what is shut aboard a ship (N4.2; held in her state since N4.1)
every man of a ship's crew: where he stands, his way, whether no way is open (N4.1)
the jobs a ship's crew is at: their places, hands told off, work left (N4.1)
the id a ship's next crew task gets (N4.1)
where a man stands when not on his way, null at his post (N4.1)
a man with no way open to his place, under which closures (N4.1)
the seconds of full-handed work a crew task has left (N4.1)
the tick a crew task's work began (N4.1)
a ship's guns packed, two whole numbers a gun in battery order: drill, load, mounting, work left; laying (N5.1)
what shot has done to a ship: her holes, lines cut, spars wounded, sails holed and men hurt (N6.1)
the shots on their way: which gun fired each and when, and what each ball has spent (N6.1)
every hole in a ship's timber: its cell, where in it, the ball, lodged or through (N6.1)
a ship's lines shot away (N6.1)
the wounds to the parts of a ship's spars (N6.1)
the shot holes in each of a ship's sails (N6.1)
a ship's men hurt and how badly (N6.1)
how much of its punch each ball of a shot in flight has spent (N6.1)
the water in a ship, t, in her larboard and starboard halves (N6.2)
where a ship's spars have broken and gone down (N6.2)
what fell and lies alongside a ship dragging her until cut away (N6.2)
the fires burning in a ship, by space (N6.2)
whether a ship still answers her helm (N6.2)
a ship's magazine has gone up (N6.2)
the holes the carpenter's crew has plugged (N6.3)
how the fight stands: when the light fails, who is beaten, and its end (N6.4)
the tick the match is drawn at (N6.4)
